references.text: Deuteronomy repeats the prohibition against kidnapping and prescribes the death penalty for anyone who steals an Israelite to make him a slave or sell him.
Joseph's brothers sold him to Midianite merchants, an example of the kidnapping and sale of a person that is forbidden in this law.
Joseph himself describes being stolen from the land of the Hebrews, which points to the crime of kidnapping.
Paul mentions "kidnappers" (ἀνδραποδισταῖς) among sinners against whom the law is directed, a direct reference to the prohibition in Exodus 21.
Revelation mentions trade in "bodies and souls of men" (σωμάτων, καὶ ψυχὰς ἀνθρώπων) as part of Babylon's sins, linked to the prohibition against human trafficking.
Highlights the unique value of a human being by contrasting the penalty for killing an animal versus killing a person.
